summary.headline: FY26 revenue grew 12.4% to 1,159 crores and EBITDA rose 24.6% to 178 crores, but reported PAT fell 4.3% to 72 crores after a 142 crore Q4 revenue deferment.
summary.overview: Management framed FY26 as a strong operating year with a Q4 shortfall: reported Q4 revenue was 273 crores, EBITDA 34 crores and PAT 0.4 crores. The shortfall was attributed to a 142 crore Q4 revenue recognition deferment (EBITDA impact above 40 crores), 11.17 crores of exceptional items linked to the divestment, and a higher tax charge versus FY25. Management signed a definitive agreement on May 26, 2026 to sell the heavy engineering, energy and automotive practice to Akkodis for USD 30.63 million, with closure expected in Q2 FY27. FY27 consolidated revenue is guided at about 1,377 crores (52% growth on the retained base), and the company reiterated its 9,000 crore FY30 revenue target.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue trending towards 1,377 crores (52% growth on retained base), covered by 927 crores under execution (including 142 crores deferred from Q4), 285 crores assured forecast visibility from design wins, and 165 crores acquisition-linked visibility.
Core-vertical EBITDA margin improvement of 150 to 200 bps YoY in FY27; core verticals already average 20%+ EBITDA margin, per management.
Margins expected to saturate around 25-27%; FY30 target of 9,000 crores revenue retained, with PAT target held and about 7,200 crores of revenue said to be enough for PAT goal at 25%+ EBITDA margin.
Phase 2 disinvestment, delayed, now targeted for H1 FY27 and expected to fund DAC, DAL, MAC and four planned acquisitions.
Recognition of the 142 crore deferred revenue expected across Q1 and Q2 FY27, subject to delivery, inspection and customer acceptance.

Extraordinary gain of about 175 crores (about 41 rupees per share EPS) expected on closure of the Akkodis divestment; ESOP pool of 3.8 million shares to be awarded by Q2 FY27 once the gain is provisioned.
Total investment plan of 2,100 to 2,250 crores, described as self-funded through restructuring; management said there are no plans for equity dilution or incremental long-term debt.
capex_capacity: DAC (Devanahalli campus) capex 1,200 crores; MAC (Missile Atmanirbhar Complex, Hyderabad) 300 crores; DAL 120 crores, of which 100 crores already spent.
Devanahalli and MAC expected to become operational through FY27, with expansion already initiated beyond them.
Acquisitions to cost roughly 600 crores; four companies planned after Phase 2 disinvestment. An aerospace manufacturing acquisition is in advanced stages, expected to start manufacturing in Q3 FY27.
Space Division established; evaluating partnerships for space bus and space payload manufacturing at Devanahalli, with infrastructure build already started.
Land systems: 20 units ready for dispatch, 25 at assembly and 85 in production under MoD contract; 120 to 140 crores cash release expected on delivery.
demand_pricing: Q4 deferment of 142 crores: 45 crores on a defense land systems program (supply chain input issue, since resolved), 84 crores on a strategic electronics program (monopolistic hardware supplier redirected output to war-related programs; materials now secured), 12.6 crores on aerospace and defense contract tied to divestment transition.
Defense pipeline includes large programs such as swarm drones and CLRTS; company says it is shortlisted for most of them.
ESAI/Xida: 3.5 million dollar order from Qualcomm; management sees a 10x revenue possibility in data centres and test equipment for hyperscalers and semiconductor firms.
Space: management cites 50-60 active Indian satellites and global demand for space bus; SAR and space payloads are focus areas, with Aldoria partnership on space situational awareness.
Make in India policy shifts have required changes to some OEM proposals; all such items subject to government approval.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 9,000 crore FY30 revenue target (about 10x from FY26) still achievable organically?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said moving from design-based revenue to design-cum-manufacturing drives a 10x to 20x uplift, and it is holding the 9,000 crore target, with momentum expected once Devanahalli and Hyderabad are ready.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins reach 20%+ in FY27, and what is the post-FY27 order book and pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said non-core verticals were margin-dilutive and targeted 150 to 200 bps YoY margin improvement in core verticals, which already average 20%+; no specific post-FY27 order book figure was given beyond pipeline comments.

qa_highlights.question: Will the engineering business transfer immediately, and is the FY30 PAT target the full potential?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a slump sale to the Akkodis India entity with people and contracts transferred and one year of handholding; guaranteed consideration of USD 23.4 million plus an earnout of USD 7.4 million tied to FY27 targets.

qa_highlights.question: How is expansion funded beyond Akkodis cash, and is equity dilution planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 2 disinvestment is expected to fully fund DAC, DAL, MAC and acquisitions; management said there are no plans for equity dilution or incremental long-term debt.

qa_highlights.question: Does reaching 9,000 crores by FY30 imply about 90% CAGR from FY28, and could higher margins lift PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins should saturate around 25-27% and revenue would scale through serial production; acquisitions buy roughly two to three years to obtain certifications and manufacturing skills.

qa_highlights.question: What is the total capex programme?
qa_highlights.answer: DAC 1,200 crores, MAC 300 crores, DAL 120 crores, and acquisitions about 600 crores, for a total of 2,100 to 2,250 crores, described as self-funded.

risks_watch: Recognition of the 142 crore deferred revenue in Q1 and Q2 FY27 depends on delivery, inspection and customer acceptance.
Phase 2 disinvestment has already slipped once and is now targeted for H1 FY27; funding of the 2,100 to 2,250 crore plan depends on it.
Receivables of 411 crores at 130 days DSO (81 days after collections) and negative operating cash flow driven by 100 crores of MoD land systems WIP, invoicing scheduled for H1 FY27.
Closure of the Akkodis divestment (Q2 FY27) and the expected 175 crore extraordinary gain; the gain drives the ESOP provisioning plan.
Execution risk on acquisitions (about 600 crores, four companies planned), government approvals, and the Make in India policy shift affecting OEM proposals.
Supply chain dependence on single or monopolistic hardware suppliers, which caused the Q4 deferment.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on the strategy, but defensive on the Q4 print; management repeatedly described the shortfall as timing and deferral rather than demand loss. Answers on the 9,000 crore target and margin path were assertive, while the funding and acquisition details were less specific and several items were described as subject to approval.
key_quotes: We did not have a bad year; we had a building year. There is a fundamental difference.
We are not shrinking; we are sharpening.
The reported PAT number should be read with this bridge rather than as a reflection of the underlying operating direction.
We have no plans for equity dilution or incremental long-term debt.
